claims: Every cyclic TPP triple in a finite 2-group with a cyclic factor of order at most eight has product of factor orders at most the group order.
A minimum-order unrestricted counterexample has three equal cyclic orders 2^e, e>=4, and group order 2^(3e-1).
The cyclic TPP inequality holds for every finite 2-group of order at most 1024.
The retained hypertope reduction gives the L034 order bound whenever a pair order is at most sixteen or the hypertope group order is at most 2^13.
new_argument: The actual characteristic top power subgroup of the normal powerful P^8 has dimension equal to the number of maximal marked coordinates. Dimension one or two forces a marked involution central by pair-generation and the order-two Sylow subgroups of GL2(F2).
induction_scope: The uniform bounded-factor result uses minimum order within the class of violating triples with a factor<=8; every smaller triple in the retained reductions still has such a factor.

retained_finite_input.result: All cyclic TPP triples in finite 2-groups of order<=256 satisfy the size bound.
retained_finite_input.role: Excludes the P^8=1 boundary, whose group order is exactly256.

retained_uniform_inputs: Phase12 powerful eighth-power subgroup and exact ordered coordinates, including its binary square-action and weak-embedding proofs.
Published powerful-group power generation and ordered factorization, through the phase11 primary-source audit.
Phase10 center-free structural bound retaining the marked isobicyclic classification.
The hypertope adapter retains flag transitivity and typed Helly, not subgroup intersection alone.

limits: The unrestricted finite 2-group cyclic TPP conjecture remains unresolved.
Equal orders are proved necessary for a minimum counterexample, not as a criterion for every individual triple.
No global multiplication-map injectivity is inferred from TPP and equality.
No new Lean module; the whole group argument is not fully formalized.
The separate top-action supplement is not part of this certificate.
